integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.title: near hit - chemical exposure at P-7110

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 1 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip was never verified as effective, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Restore the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels on P-7110, M-7110 and PT-7110 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically setting and proving mechanical seal support systems. P-7110 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during transfer operations while the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels was in place but did not perform. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 22 December 2006 a near hit was recorded on P-7110, M-7110 and PT-7110 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during transfer operations; chemical energy held as hydrocarbon was not released.
